newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela, Japan weeks away from Venalum agreement.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela, Japan weeks away from Venalum agreement.

text.p: Venezuela is still weeks away from reaching a final agreement with the Japanese shareholders of aluminum smelter Venalum, Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) President Alberto Poletto said on Friday.
Despite reaching a preliminary agreement to reduce the Japanese consortium's veto powers, the two sides have yet to agree on the size of compensation.
"This compensation should be calculated and defined in the next few weeks. We are working on it," Poletto told reporters.
A deal to reduce the Japanese veto power will include the reinitiating of a supply contract for 20 percent of Venalum's annual production.
The supply contract of 90,000 tonnes per year was suspended in February in an effort to pressure the Japanese to give up the veto powers.

Poletto confirmed newspaper reports the Japanese consortium, which owns 20 percent of Venalum, had asked for $50 million in compensation for the veto rights. But any cash payment would have to be made by an eventual buyer of Venalum, he said.
The government plans to sell Venalum, together with smelter Alcasa, carbon anode manufacturer Carbonorca and bauxite/alumina manufacturer Bauxilum before the end of the year.
Poletto said the sale, for which 13 companies have qualified to bid, would leave the state with a small holding in the aluminum sector.
"We have decided to sell everything. There are no half measures here. We will only reserve 10 percent of shares with the express purpose of placing them on the local stock market," he said.
"The important thing is we have agreed to the manner in which the statutes had to be modified to make the package attractive to investors," he added.

The Japanese consortium which holds a 20 percent stake in Venalum includes Showa Denko KK, Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp.
